title: Italian Bean and Vegetable Soup with Small Pasta and Basil
summary: A thick, rustic Italian soup of leek, carrot, courgette, cannellini beans and small pasta in a light tomato broth, finished with fresh basil, grated cheese and a drizzle of good olive oil. Hearty enough for a meal on its own.
equipment: large heavy-based pot with a lid (at least 5 litres)

ingredients.item: leek, white and pale green part, sliced and washed
celery stalks, cut into 1 cm dice
medium potato, cut into 1.5 cm dice
fine sea salt or table salt
can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed (240 g drained)
Parmesan-style hard cheese, finely grated, to serve (animal-rennet-free)

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat and cook the onion, leek, carrots and celery with a pinch of the salt for 10 minutes, stirring, until soft but not browned. Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute. Cooking slowly without colour draws out the vegetables' natural sweetness for a gentle, mellow base.

steps.title: Simmer with potato
steps.text: Add the potato, tomatoes, water, remaining salt and pepper, then bring to the boil. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the potato is tender. Some of the potato starch seeps into the broth, giving the soup a fuller body.

steps.title: Add beans and pasta
steps.text: Stir in the courgette, beans and pasta and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so the pasta does not stick to the base, until the pasta is tender. Then add the spinach for 1 minute until wilted and the soup is boiling hot. If it looks very thick, loosen it with a splash of water, since the pasta absorbs liquid as it cooks.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in most of the basil, ladle the soup into bowls and top with the cheese, the remaining basil and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil. Adding basil at the end keeps its sweet, peppery aroma, which fades with long cooking.

tips: A common mistake is letting the pasta sit on the base of the pot, where it sticks and scorches; stir now and then while it simmers.
Choose an animal-rennet-free Parmesan-style cheese if you need one.
Rinse the canned beans well to remove the starchy liquid, which can make the soup cloudy and gluey.
The soup thickens as it stands, so keep some hot water handy to adjust.
storage: Cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 4 days; the pasta softens and thickens the soup, so add water when reheating. Reheat until boiling hot (74°C).
